svg.title: Identify strand role before transcribing a sequence
svg.desc: Coding DNA5′-ATG GAA TTT TAA-3′ aligns with template3′-TAC CTT AAA ATT-5′ and gives RNA5′-AUG GAA UUU UAA-3′. RNA polymerase reads the template3′→5′ while extending RNA5′→3′; coding DNA matches the RNA except T versus U. A separate explicitly coding fragment5′-TAC ACA TGC ATC-3′ produces5′-UAC ACA UGC AUC-3′, with Tyr–Thr–Cys–Ile only under a stipulated first-base translated frame. The fragment alone supplies no complete initiation context. Promoter orientation determines which strand serves as template for a gene. Sequence role cannot be reversed merely because TAC resembles a familiar start-template example, and sequence prediction does not measure RNA or protein abundance.

g.text: Identify strand role before transcribing a sequence
Exact existing teaching sequences keep complementing and reversing as separate operations.
Template read 3′→5′; RNA synthesized 5′→3′. Coding strand is not the template.
Check a different explicitly CODING fragment: 5′-TAC ACA TGC ATC-3′.
Corresponding RNA: 5′-UAC ACA UGC AUC-3′, not its complementary RNA sequence.
With the stipulated first-base translated frame: Tyr–Thr–Cys–Ile; initiation context is not supplied.
Promoter/gene orientation determines the template; a chromosome strand is not always “the template.”
Sequence prediction does not measure transcript abundance or prove functional protein production.
